One set of blood cultures was sent within 6 hours of admission during the haemodialysis session with samples from the haemodialysis circuit. These sets included one aerobic (BD Bactec Plus Aerobic/F medium) and one anaerobic bottle (BD BACTEC Lytic Anaerobic medium) each and were analysed using the Bactec FX 200 Automated Blood Culture System at 36°C and were negative for aerobes, anaerobes and yeasts after 2 and 7 days of incubation.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Metastatic methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection with infective endocarditis, pulmonary septic emboli, axillary abscess with a subacute presentation in a patient with chronic end-stage kidney disease on maintenance haemodialysis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old male with end-stage chronic kidney disease on maintenance hemodialysis (6 months duration) via cuffed tunnelled right internal jugular vein catheter presented with a 3-week history of intermittent low to moderate-grade fever, night sweats, generalized weakness, exertional breathlessness, mild cough, loss of appetite, and left axillary pain for 2 days. Recent left brachiocephalic arteriovenous fistula surgery 1 month prior served as a likely source of bacteremia. Initial blood cultures obtained within 6 hours of admission were negative. However, echocardiography (transthoracic and transoesophageal) revealed multiple tiny vegetations at the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve on the atrial side with near moderate tricuspid regurgitation, confirming infective endocarditis. Chest CT with contrast demonstrated left loculated hydropneumothorax with multiple cavitary nodules and reverse halo signs, consistent with pulmonary septic emboli. On day 4 of admission, ultrasound-guided percutaneous aspiration of a small (5 cc) irregularly shaped collection in the left axilla yielded gram-positive bacteria on microscopy. Subsequent culture of the axillary aspirate identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) sensitive to clindamycin, vancomycin, linezolid, and ciprofloxacin. Laboratory investigations on admission showed significant leucocytosis (WBC 16,000/mL) with neutrophilia. The clinical presentation, imaging findings, and microbiological confirmation from the axillary abscess established the diagnosis of metastatic MRSA infection with hematogenous dissemination to the heart (endocarditis), lungs (septic emboli), and left axilla (abscess formation).
